title: How Local Service Businesses Get Into Google's Map Pack (2026)
description: The 3 ranking levers that actually move you into Google's local 3-pack — and how to automate the website and content work behind them.
primary_keyword: how to get into google map pack
author: Jack Bates
answer: To land in Google's Map Pack you need three things working together: a fully-optimized Google Business Profile, consistent reviews, and a website with dedicated service-and-city pages that prove local relevance. The first two are manual; the third is where automation does the heavy lifting.
body_html:
The Map Pack — those top three businesses with the little map above the regular results — is where local customers actually click. Ranking there isn't luck, and it isn't a single trick. It's three levers pulled at the same time.

The three levers that move the Map Pack

LeverWhat it isEffort
Google Business ProfileCategories, services, photos, hours, postsManual, ongoing
ReviewsSteady velocity + repliesManual, ongoing
Website relevanceA page for every service in every city you serveAutomatable

Why the website is the unfair advantage

Most local businesses have one generic "Services" page. Google can't tell whether you actually serve a given town, so it ranks the competitor who has a real page for it. The fix is a page per service per city — "emergency electrician in Brandon," "panel upgrades in Riverview," and so on. Building those by hand is brutal. Building them with a system is a weekend.

How we automate it

At Bates Media we build the site, generate the service-and-city pages with proper local content and schema, optimize every page for on-page and AI search, and wire up the reviews-and-leads automation behind it — so the three levers stay pulled without you touching a thing.

faq.q: How long does it take to rank in the Map Pack?
faq.a: Usually 2–4 months for competitive local terms once the Google Business Profile, reviews, and service-area pages are all in place. Less competitive towns can move in weeks.

faq.q: Do I need a separate page for every city?
faq.a: For the services and towns you actually want to rank in, yes. Distinct, genuinely-local pages are how Google confirms you serve that area — but they must be unique and useful, not duplicated templates.
The website and content side, yes — research, page generation, and on-page/AI optimization all automate. Reviews and your Google Business Profile still need a human touch.
